chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn al-Jahm entered upon Abū al-Ḥasan Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام while he had dyed himself with black dye, and he said:

“Indeed, there is reward in dyeing, and dyeing and grooming are among the things by which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, increases the chastity of women. Some women have indeed abandoned chastity because their husbands abandoned grooming.”
He said to him, “It has reached us that henna increases gray hair.” He said, “What thing increases gray hair, while gray hair increases every day?”

key_terms.أَجْرًا: reward from Allah for the act mentioned
key_terms.أَزْوَاجِهِنَّ: their husbands, whose grooming affects marital relations
key_terms.ٱلتَّهْيِئَةُ: grooming and self-preparation in one's appearance
key_terms.ٱلشَّيْبِ: gray hair or whiteness of hair due to age
key_terms.ٱلنِّسَاءِ: women, specifically in the marital context of the narration
key_terms.ٱلْخِضَابِ: dyeing the hair; an act described here as carrying reward

ai.seo_question: What does Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام say about hair dyeing, grooming, and their effect on marital chastity?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that personal grooming, including dyeing the hair, carries reward and has moral and social benefits within marriage. Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام links a husband's self-care with preserving a wife's chastity and dismisses the notion that henna causes gray hair to increase.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.276 - Al-Hasan ibn al-Jahm entered upon Abu Al-Hasan Imam Musa ibn Jafar Al-Kadhim (as) who had dyed his hair with black dye.
Imam (as) said: "Indeed, there is a reward in dyeing. Dyeing and grooming are among those things which increase the chastity of women, and some women have abandoned chastity because their husbands have neglected grooming themselves."
(ibn Al-Jahm) replied to Him: "We have heard that henna increases gray hair?”
Imam (as) said: “What increases gray hair? Gray hair increases every day."
